source_title: ‘Mad Max’ Actor Richard Norton Cause of Death Revealed to Be Linked to Peptide Usage - People.com
source_excerpt:
The actor died on March 30, 2025, after self-administering a new peptide therapy
A coroner’s report revealed Richard Norton died on March 30, 2025, after self-administering a new peptide therapy
The report noted that the actor “had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner”
Norton appeared in more than 70 films and choreographed stunts for Mad Max: Fury Road and Suicide Squad
Richard Norton ’s cause of death has been revealed more than a year after his death.
According to a newly released coroner’s report obtained by PEOPLE, the Australian martial artist and actor died on March 30, 2025, at the age of 75 as a result of “a cardiac arrest at home following self- administration of recently commenced peptide therapy.”
“Injections of some types of peptides are increasingly being used in sports performance to increase healing and muscle growth. However, they are not approved by the TGA [Therapeutic Goods Administration] or any global regulatory authority for human use,” per the coroner’s report.
According to the document, the use of peptides in this context “are mostly considered experimental in humans” and their “toxicology is largely unknown.”
Two weeks before his death, Norton told his medical practitioner that he was interested in peptide therapy, adding that he had already taken the protein with a previous doctor for “fatigue, reduced physical recovery, shoulder pain and loss of lean muscle mass,” according to the report.
He and the medical practitioner discussed the risks, and blood tests were administered. He was approved for peptide therapy on March 19.
They acknowledged that “the treatment is recognised as experimental and prescribed off-label, but it is done so under close clinical supervision, with ongoing monitoring and consideration of individual patient needs and responses.”
On March 25, Norton told his medical practitioner that he was feeling good and that the treatment was working, per the coroner’s report.
Three days later, Norton reached out to a nurse at his doctor’s office, claiming he “had dropped and broken” the vial of his treatment “and requested a replacement,” which was issued. He was also given two additional peptides.
At the time, he noted to his nurse that he was administering double the prescribed dose, and the nurse advised him to only take the prescribed amount.
At approximately 9:00 p.m. that evening, his wife, Judy Green, reported that Norton felt “hot and flushed and then collapsed and became unresponsive” after administering his second dose of peptides that day.
She first contacted her doctor before contacting emergency services and provided CPR to her husband until medics arrived just before 9:30 p.m.
He was taken to the hospital where his “tryptase and troponin levels were noted to be elevated.” Clinicians noted that the actor suffered from a cardiac arrest after experiencing anaphylaxis following the peptide injection. He died on March 30, 2025, at 10:17 a.m.

“I am numb and devastated, I have no words I have lost my everything,” Green wrote in the caption under a post on her husband’s Instagram account announcing his death.
Throughout his career, Norton starred in over 70 movies, working alongside actors like Chuck Norris and Jackie Chan . He also choreographed stunts for projects like Mad Max: Fury Road and Suicide Squad .
